info.name: Apiconfy
info.description:
API collection for Apiconfy integration runtime.

## Setup
1. Start the server with `pnpm dev` (install dependencies with pnpm only).
2. Set base_url (default http://localhost:3000) and api_key if API_KEY is configured.
3. REST > Invoke folders run in order: registration, invocation, execution lookup. Invoke scripts save execution_id.
4. Complex/error examples use upstream_url (default https://httpbin.org). Use dummy data only, or your own httpbin-compatible upstream.

## Structure — by component type
Health and Service Management retain existing requests. REST includes registration plus Phase 2 Invoke > Simple Examples, Complex Examples, Error Cases. Existing full auth/TLS/circuitBreaker registrations are registration-only; invoking them returns 501. Runnable Phase 2 complex examples include every supported section and intentionally omit unsupported capabilities. Mapper, Database, Script and SQS are future Phase 11 designs, not registered handlers in Phase 2; Scheduler is Phase 10.

## Data bag
Input uses {$context.*}; ephemeral raw upstream response uses {$output.*}. Response transformations wrap output under unique keys. Phase 2 returns transformed output directly and leaves context.output empty; callers must not supply context.output. Transformation still runs on failure: wire data is null, while GET /api/v1/executions/{{execution_id}} exposes the sanitized transformed, error-injected result. Merging into {$context.output.<uniqueKey>} is Phase 5 workflow behavior.

## Limits
Only timeout.response is enforced, per attempt through body consumption. Auth, custom TLS/disableSSL=true, connect/socket/idle, circuitBreaker and unsupported content types return 501. Rate limiting is an in-memory per-process token bucket (429 plus Retry-After); shared DB-backed limits are Phase 4 using the configured SQLite/PostgreSQL DBAdapter, never Redis/Couchbase. Phase 2 implementation verification is pending; this collection is not test-run evidence.

item.name: REST
item.description: REST is the only implemented component type. Existing Complex Examples with auth, TLS, circuitBreaker or connect/socket/idle timeouts are REGISTRATION-ONLY: invocation returns 501. Invoke contains runnable Phase 2 examples with every supported config section; unsupported sections are intentionally omitted. Phase 2 final verification is pending. Never send real secrets to the public example upstream.

item.name: Invoke
item.description: Run each folder in order: register before invoke. Simple Examples use local /health. Complex and selected error examples require an httpbin-compatible upstream_url; default is public httpbin.org, so use dummy data only. Each invoke saves execution_id. Failure data is null on the wire; execution lookup exposes the sanitized transformed error-injected result. No workflow context merge in Phase 2.

request.description: Minimal required REST config: request.uri and request.method only. Returns 201 on create or 200 on upsert. base_url must also be reachable from the Apiconfy server.
Expected 200 success, raw health body under data, meta.executionId and durationMs. Saves execution_id; one dispatch attempt.
Expected 200; data.type=service, status=COMPLETED, attempts=1. Recording is awaited best-effort; a failed DB write can leave a 404.

item.name: Complex Examples
item.description: Includes all executable Phase 2 sections. Auth, SSL, circuitBreaker and connect/socket/idle are deliberately absent because they would make these registrations non-executable. See REST > Complex Examples for registration-only full future configurations.

item.name: 1. Register mapped echo with retry and rate limit

request.description: Expected 201/200. Validation precedes default, so default cannot rescue a failed rule. Unique echoResponse key prevents future workflow collisions. No real credentials are used.
Expected 200; data.echoResponse preserves mapped JSON values. Raw response is audited; transformed output is persisted as execution result. X-Execution-Id is propagated upstream.
Expected 200, skippedExecution=true, data=null. No upstream request, no env resolution, no limiter token; persisted attempts=0.
Expected 201/200. Every supported section is shown; unsupported auth/TLS/circuitBreaker blocks are omitted. Form bodies are serialized with URLSearchParams.
Expected 200; data.formEchoResponse.label round-trips spaces, ampersand and plus.
Expected 201/200. GET ignores payloadTemplate; all supported sections are shown. The true validation rule permits a 204 body, then default resolves context before transformation reads response.
Expected 200, data.defaultResponse={status:empty,customerId:demo-123}. Upstream status 204 still becomes a normal invocation envelope.
Inspect sanitized result/context and real dispatch attempts.

item.name: Error Cases
item.description: Run in order. Expected statuses are in request names. Upstream-dependent examples need httpbin-compatible upstream_url. The 429 pair must run within 60 seconds; reruns may already be limited until refill or server restart. Schema-valid unsupported configurations are intentionally registration-only until invoked here to demonstrate 501.

request.description: VALIDATION_FAILED before execution. Do not expect a persisted invocation for an invalid request body.
VALIDATION_FAILED: output is reserved even when empty.
Expected 201/200. Valid predicate intentionally fails after local health response.
Expected 200, FAILED, attempts=1; transformed result includes raw health under wrapper.upstream plus standardized error.
Expected 201/200. One process-local token. Re-registration is not a promise to reset the bucket.
200 on a fresh/refilled bucket. Immediately run the next request.
Expected 201/200. Registration-only capability; env references are masked. No environment variables need setting: the invocation guard runs before env resolution.
Expected 201/200. Schema-valid but not executable in Phase 2.
NOT_IMPLEMENTED, attempts=0. socket/idle and circuitBreaker/custom SSL are guarded similarly.

item.name: Complex Examples
item.description: Registration-only full REST configurations. Auth/TLS/connect/socket/idle and circuitBreaker remain unsupported at invocation (501). Use REST > Invoke > Complex Examples for runnable Phase 2 scenarios; these existing registrations are preserved as future-capability references.

item.name: Register — full-featured REST with auth, retry, transformation

request.description:
Full-featured REST component showing:
- OAuth2 auth with `$env.` references (masked in response)
- Retry with exponential backoff
- Timeout config
- Dynamic headers from `{$context.*}`
- Payload template with context mapping
- Response validation rules
- Response transformation wraps output under unique key `createOrderResponse`
- Condition for conditional execution
- Metadata
Send the same (service, action) again to upsert. Returns 200 (not 201) on update. Includes response validation and transformation wraps output under unique key `createOrderResponse`.
Returns 400 with `VALIDATION_FAILED` and field-level details.
Returns 400 — `request.uri` is required for REST components.
Returns 400 — request.method must be GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE.
Returns 400 — `request.disableSSL` and `request.ssl` are mutually exclusive.
